Mr. Anderson is seen throwing a series of punches at the victim
His injuries included a cut above his left eye and on his left cheek

police located a restricted firearm, a pistol, in a boot in the vehicle
rationale_highlights: significant Gladue factors have permeated every area of Mr. Anderson's life
systemic racism and the legacy of colonialism have had a direct impact on Mr. Anderson's life, to the extent that a court can find that his moral blameworthiness is reduced
the impact of Gladue factors on the sentence to be imposed must still be a weighty one

crime_highlights: Mr. Evans offered M.L. some drugs
After inhaling from the bong, M.L. lost consciousness
Mr. Evans had sexual intercourse with M.L. while she was unconscious
Given her incapacity, M.L. could not and did not consent to the sexual activity with Mr. Evans
rationale_highlights: I accept the findings set out in Mr. Evans' Indigenous Sentencing Report to the effect that there are certain factors present in the concentric circles of his community, family, and personal life that impact upon his moral blameworthiness
Mr. Evans was placed in the care of many different relatives, impacting his ability to develop a moral foundation for discerning right from wrong
weighing all of the aggravating and mitigating factors just discussed, I find that a fit and just sentence for Mr. Evans is a custodial one with a duration of three years
note: Court says factors impact moral blameworthiness; no explicit reduction statement.

rationale_highlights: it is necessary for the Crown to consider the offender’s aboriginal status in determining whether to request a mandatory minimum sentence of imprisonment
the inference follows that Mr. Anderson’s aboriginal status was not taken into account when the determination was made to seek the mandatory minimum sentence
the trial judge clearly took into account Mr. Anderson’s aboriginal status
note: Appeal on Crown discretion; no narrative of offence beyond para 39; no culpability reduction stated.
